headline: Revenue and margins climb; heavy buybacks drain equity
summary_short: Paycom's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose to $572M (+5.1% q/q, +7.8% y/y) and net income jumped 36.8% q/q to $156M ($3.04 diluted EPS), while $1,070.8M of share buybacks funded partly by a new $675.0M revolver draw cut stockholders' equity roughly in half.
summary_long: Revenue reached $572M (+5.1% q/q, +7.8% y/y) on new clients, cross-sell, usage growth and pricing, partly offset by small-client attrition. Opex rose just 4.7% against 7.8% revenue growth, lifting operating margin to 36.8% and operating income to $210M (+13.5% y/y). Net income rose 11.8% y/y to $156M ($3.04 diluted GAAP EPS, $3.15 non-GAAP), aided by a $9.0M naming-rights gain despite a higher 27.7% tax rate. Paycom repurchased $1,070.8M of stock and drew $675.0M on its revolver, cutting equity to $812M and cash to $154M. FY2026 guidance: $2.175-2.195B revenue, $950-970M Adjusted EBITDA, provided without an explicit raise/hold signal.

drivers.explanation: CEO Chad Richison attributed the quarter to executing on "full-solution automation, stronger client ROI achievement and world-class service."
Growth came from new-client additions, added applications and usage on existing clients, and pricing, partially offset by attrition concentrated among smaller clients.
Operating income grew faster than revenue because total operating expenses rose only 4.7% versus 7.8% revenue growth, expanding operating margin to 36.8% from 34.9%.
A $9.0 million other-income gain from the naming-rights agreement amendment added to net income, despite a higher 27.7% effective tax rate versus 26.8% a year ago.
EPS grew faster than net income because diluted weighted-average shares fell about 9% y/y to 51.2 million as buybacks reduced share count.
Purchases of property and equipment fell $6.5 million from the prior-year quarter, per the MD&A's investing-activities discussion.
Treasury stock rose $1,070.8 million on buybacks, partly funded by a new $675.0 million revolver draw, mechanically shrinking total stockholders' equity despite positive net income.
Cash fell as $1,070.8 million of buybacks and dividends were funded from operating cash flow and revolver borrowings rather than accumulating cash.
